# `silk/schema/yaml`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read and write `Schema` types as YAML.

## When to use
Call [`SchemaYaml.decode`](#SchemaYaml.impl.decode) to read a value of a `silk.schema.schema.Schema` type from YAML text,
such as a configuration file, [`SchemaYaml.decodeAll`](#SchemaYaml.impl.decodeAll) to report every problem in the text at
once, and [`SchemaYaml.encode`](#SchemaYaml.impl.encode) to write a value as YAML to the ambient `Writer`. Show the
problems with `silk.schema.report.SchemaReport`. Use `silk.yaml.document.YamlDocument` to work
with YAML whose shape is not known in advance.

## Details
Decoding parses the text into a `YamlDocument` first, then reads the value from it, so members
may come in any order. Members the type does not name are skipped, or reported when its spec is
`Spec.strict`. Every problem carries the span of the bytes it is about. A field that holds text
also accepts a plain scalar that YAML reads as another kind, such as `version: 1.10` or
`zip: 01234`, and gets its text exactly as written. Encoding writes block-style YAML, with struct
fields in declaration order.

## Examples
### Read a configuration file
```silk
import silk.collections.list { List }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.schema.issue { SchemaError }
import silk.schema.schema { Schema }
import silk.schema.yaml { SchemaYaml }
import silk.text.string { String }

struct Service {
  pub name: String,
  pub version: String,
  pub ports: List<u16>,
}

impl Schema for Service {}

effect fn load() -> i32 ! SchemaError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let api = run SchemaYaml.decode<Service>(b"name: api\nversion: 1.10\nports: [80, 443]\n")
  if api.name.view() != "api" || api.version.view() != "1.10" || List<u16>.get(&api.ports, 1) != 443 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! SchemaError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run load() |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

Import as `SchemaYaml` with `import silk.schema.yaml { SchemaYaml }`.

<a id="SchemaYaml.impl.decode"></a>

### Associated function `decode`

```silk
pub effect fn decode<T: Schema>(bytes: &[u8]) -> T ! SchemaError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Reads one value of type `T` from the YAML text `bytes`, stopping at the first problem.

#### Details

The text must hold one YAML document. A text field also accepts a plain scalar that YAML reads
as a number, a boolean, or null, and gets the text as written.

#### Errors

- `SchemaError` if the text is not valid YAML, holds more than one document, or does not hold
  a `T`. Its `path` names the part that failed, and its issue has the span of the bytes it is
  about. Invalid YAML gives `IssueReason.InvalidSyntax`.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the document or the value.

<a id="SchemaYaml.impl.decodeAll"></a>

### Associated function `decodeAll`

```silk
pub effect fn decodeAll<T: Schema>(bytes: &[u8]) -> T ! SchemaErrors | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Reads one value of type `T` from the YAML text `bytes`, reporting every problem.

#### Details

A field, element or variant that fails is recorded and skipped, and reading goes on with the
next one, so one call lists every problem, in input order: a missing key, a wrong type, a
number out of range and a failed rule alike. Text that is not valid YAML is the one problem
reported. At most `MAX_PROBLEMS` (64) are listed.

#### Errors

- `SchemaErrors` with every problem found.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the document or the value.

<a id="SchemaYaml.impl.encode"></a>

### Associated function `encode`

```silk
pub effect fn encode<T: Schema>(value: &T)
    -> () ! SchemaError | WriterError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Writer | &mut Allocator
```

Writes `value` as block-style YAML to the ambient `Writer`.

#### Details

Struct fields are written in declaration order, nested collections are indented by two
spaces, and strings are quoted only when a reader would read them as something else. The text
goes to the `Writer` in pieces of up to 4 KiB. It does not flush the `Writer`.

#### Errors

- `SchemaError` if the value nests more than 128 levels deep. Its path is empty.
- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails. Bytes that it accepted before the failure stay written.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if a codec needs memory that the `Allocator` cannot supply.

#### Examples

```silk
import silk.collections.slice { Slice }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.io.writer { Writer, WriterError }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.schema.issue { SchemaError }
import silk.schema.schema { Schema }
import silk.schema.yaml { SchemaYaml }

struct Limits {
  pub retries: u8,
}

impl Schema for Limits {}

struct Server {
  pub port: u16,
  pub limits: Limits,
}

impl Schema for Server {}

struct Capture {
  bytes: [u8; 64],
  length: usize,
}

impl Writer for Capture {
  effect fn writeAll(self: &mut Self, val: &[u8]) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer {
    Slice.copyInto<u8>(&mut self.bytes, self.length, val)
    self.length = self.length + val.length
    return ()
  }
  effect fn flush(self: &mut Self) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer { return () }
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! SchemaError | WriterError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut capture = Capture {bytes: [0; 64], length: 0}
  let server = Server {port: 8080, limits: Limits {retries: 3}}
  run SchemaYaml.encode<Server>(&server) |> Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut capture)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  if Slice.view<u8>(&capture.bytes, 0, capture.length) != b"port: 8080\nlimits:\n  retries: 3\n" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="YamlSchemaReader"></a>

## `YamlSchemaReader`

```silk
pub struct YamlSchemaReader<'document>
```

A `SchemaReader` over a node of a parsed `silk.yaml.document.YamlDocument`.

### When to use

[`SchemaYaml.decode`](#SchemaYaml.impl.decode) uses it. Use it directly to read a typed value from one node of a document
that the program parsed itself, such as one document of a stream from
`YamlDocument.parseAll`: call `Schemas.read` with it.

### Details

A text field also accepts a plain scalar that YAML reads as a number, a boolean, or null, and
gets the text as written. Spans in the problems are byte positions in the parsed text.

<a id="YamlSchemaWriter"></a>

## `YamlSchemaWriter`

```silk
pub struct YamlSchemaWriter
```

A `SchemaWriter` that writes block-style YAML to the ambient `Writer`.

### When to use

[`SchemaYaml.encode`](#SchemaYaml.impl.encode) uses it. Use it directly to write several values as the documents of one
stream: call `Schemas.write` for each, `nextDocument` between them, and `finish` at the end.

### Gotchas

The text is kept in a 4 KiB buffer; call `finish` after the last value, or the end of the text
stays in it.

<a id="YamlSchemaWriter.impl"></a>

```silk
pub effect fn finish(self: &mut Self) -> () ! Issue | WriterError ? &mut Writer
```

Writes the rest of the buffer to the `Writer`. It does not flush the `Writer`.

#### Errors

- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails. Bytes that it accepted before the failure stay written.
